acceptance.given: A matrix aggregate is evaluated and its evidence manifest marks one or more required matrix cases as non-executed.

oracle.expected: Aggregate status is invalid and records the non-executed case identifiers as the invalidation reason.
forbidden: Aggregate is valid or accepted when any required matrix evidence is non-executed.
oracle.observable: Validator output contains invalid aggregate status with explicit non-executed evidence references.

acceptance.then: Run the aggregate validator against a manifest containing a non-executed matrix case and inspect its emitted status and reason.
acceptance.when: During aggregate evaluation after matrix-case execution status has been resolved.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select aggregate evaluation with required matrix evidence marked non-executed; expect validation to fail if it accepts the aggregate.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Aggregate evaluation invalidates whenever matrix evidence is confirmed non-executed and emits the affected case identifiers.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve the existing aggregate result schema; rollback restores prior validator logic.

slice_hint.state_transition: evaluating -> invalidated when any required matrix case is non-executed.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Validator emits invalid aggregate status with explicit non-executed matrix evidence references.

acceptance.given: A verdict is produced by Toolchain semantic evaluation with a current source identity available.

oracle.expected: The verdict artifact contains a traceable current source identity and execution provenance resolvable to the exact evaluated source.
forbidden: Verdict omits current source identity or relies only on assistant prose or historical identity.
oracle.observable: Parsed verdict JSON records current source identity and a resolvable source reference.

acceptance.then: Parse the verdict artifact and resolve its source identity against the current source manifest.
acceptance.when: After each verdict is produced and before it is authorized for consumption.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select verdict output whose source identity is missing, stale, or unresolved; expect provenance validation to fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Verdict generation and validation bind every verdict to current source identity and real execution provenance, rejecting untraceable or prose-only results.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Keep verdict artifact fields backward compatible; rollback removes only provenance enforcement.

slice_hint.terminal_predicate: A parsed verdict resolves current source identity and real execution provenance; otherwise validation fails.

acceptance.given: A pre-repair baseline captures historical repository-relative paths and repair execution has completed.

oracle.expected: Post-repair comparison reports the historical repository-relative path set and values are identical to baseline.
forbidden: Any historical path is renamed, moved, deleted, or changed during repair.
oracle.observable: Deterministic path-manifest diff is empty for all historical entries.

acceptance.then: Generate deterministic pre/post repository-relative path manifests and assert an empty historical diff.
acceptance.when: During repair verification after the candidate change is applied.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select a repair that renames or moves a historical repository-relative path; expect path-manifest comparison to fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Repair verification preserves every historical repository-relative path and rejects rename, move, deletion, or spelling changes.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Path manifests remain compatible; rollback restores prior repair behavior while retaining historical files.

slice_hint.state_transition: baseline captured -> repair applied -> path manifest compared.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Historical path manifest comparison completes with zero differences.

acceptance.given: The FR-10 enable/disable/behavioral-rollback/re-enable flow is executed for each applicable Consumer selected by the current Consumer Manifest.

oracle.expected: Each applicable Consumer has a recorded completed re-enable operation invoked through its repository real call surface, with no simulated or indirect substitute.
forbidden: Any applicable Consumer lacks a re-enable call record.
Re-enable is performed only through a simulated, indirect, or nonexistent call surface.
oracle.observable: Per-Consumer execution evidence includes call-surface identity and completed re-enable result.

acceptance.then: Inspect per-Consumer execution evidence and verify each re-enable event resolves to an actual callable repository function or command.
acceptance.when: After the complete FR-10 flow finishes for all applicable Consumers.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select an applicable Consumer whose re-enable is simulated, indirect, or absent; expect the real-call-surface assertion to fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: The FR-10 flow executes re-enable for every applicable Consumer through a real repository call surface and records completion per Consumer.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Consumer Manifest and execution evidence schemas remain compatible; rollback restores dispatch behavior without deleting evidence.

slice_hint.state_transition: consumer pending re-enable -> real call invoked -> completed re-enable recorded.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: All applicable Consumer entries have completed re-enable evidence bound to a real call-surface identity.
